metadata.body:
# PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

Blueprint for clio-agent. The numeric work lives in plain scripts in this
repository so it can run on PBS compute nodes without an LLM:

- `agent/manifest.py`: list the DASV records on `s3://nrel-pds-porotomo/` and sample them.
- `agent/detect.py`: per-record detector (common-mode removal, 10-150 Hz band-pass, median STA/LTA).
- `agent/pbs/submit.sh`: submit the distributed detection plus aggregation job to Aurora.
- `agent/hazard.py`: anomaly z-scores, event catalogue, pumping volumes, seismogenic index, probabilities.

The experts orchestrate those scripts, inspect files, and explain results. They
never make up numbers. Every figure they report comes from `summary.json` or a
tool result.

Install by linking this directory into `~/.config/clio-agent/agent-blueprints/`.

agent_blueprint.name: PoroTomo Induced-Seismicity Agent

session.title: porotomo-induced-seismicity: Report the headline results of the agent

answer:
HEADLINE RESULTS — run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (read-only report; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run; all numbers quoted verbatim from summary.json, cross-checked against record counts in anomalies.csv / events.csv / detect_rank*.jsonl).

RUN SCOPE
- Records analysed: 759 (all status "ok"), selected at stride 20 from 15,164 total records (sampled fraction of time 0.03314), spanning 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z; mean 2003.99 ms per record.
- Anomalous records: 57 (z_threshold = 5.0).
- DAS detections: 62 events in 53 records; scaled to full time = 1870.77; relative b = 0.984935, mc_relative = -0.849246, 34 events above mc.

SEISMOGENIC INDEX Sigma
- hazard_catalog_based: b=1.0 -> Sigma = -5.448901270028832; b=0.73 -> Sigma = -5.3193012700288325; b=0.65 -> Sigma = -5.280901270028833.
- hazard_das_upper_bound: Sigma = -2.698279919032152 (b_used = 0.9849352475487246, DAS relative-magnitude Aki MLE).

P(Mw>=5.5) PER YEAR (at observed rate) — CALIBRATED estimate (hazard_catalog_based, calibrated against the LBNL/NCEDC March 2016 catalogue, GDR 859, calibrated ML magnitudes):
- b=1.0: 0.00011982478978644906 (~1.2e-4 per year)
- b=0.73: 0.004921548824626587 (~4.9e-3 per year)
- b=0.65: 0.014735103451029574 (~1.5e-2 per year)
(For reference, P(Mw>=5.5) over the observed volume: b=1.0 -> 5.2356e-06; b=0.73 -> 2.1554e-04; b=0.65 -> 6.4838e-04.)

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (hazard_das_upper_bound) — NOT calibrated; an upper bound that over-counts because every DAS detection is treated as an event at/above the catalogue minimum magnitude using uncalibrated relative magnitudes:
- P(Mw>=5.5) per year = 0.07842182774171746 (~7.8e-2 per year)
- P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume = 0.0024076054468051833

WHICH IS WHICH: The catalog-based probabilities (the per-b values above) are the CALIBRATED estimates, anchored to the LBNL/NCEDC March 2016 catalogue (5 events, mc = -0.48, mag_max = 0.07, ML). The DAS-based value is an UPPER BOUND with uncalibrated magnitudes and should only be quoted with that caveat.

ASSUMPTIONS: Shapiro et al. (2021) Eq. 5, P = 1 - exp(-V * 10^(Sigma - b*M)); pumping context from GDR 917 corrected deployment data. Note: interpretation.md carries a reviewer flag that its own prose mislabels the stride and which estimate is calibrated; summary.json and the governing instructions are authoritative (catalog-based = calibrated; DAS = upper bound that over-counts).
